card.statement:
In view of Remark 1, we can express the condition in
terms of $\mathbf{M}(V^{\prime})$ : we set
$\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}_{\infty}=-\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}(\dim V)$ . Then $\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}$ is
extended to a function ${\mathbb{Z}}^{Q_{0}\sqcup\{\infty\}}\to{\mathbb{R}}$ . Then the
condition is equivalent to $\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}(\dim S^{\prime})\leq 0$ for a graded
invariant subspace $S^{\prime}\subset V^{\prime}$ . According to either
$S^{\prime}_{\infty}=0$ or ${\mathbb{C}}$ , we have the above two cases (1), (2)
respectively. Note that $S^{\prime}$ being invariant means $S^{\prime}$ is a
submodule. Hence this reformulation coincides with the standard
King’s stability condition [Ki94].

Let us give a simple consequence of the $\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}$ -stability
condition. It basically says a $\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}$ -stable framed
representation is Schur:
card.label: Remark 7

paper.title: Introduction to quiver varieties -- for ring and representation theoriests
paper.abstract: We review the definition of quiver varieties and their relation to representation theory of Kac-Moody Lie algebras. Target readers are ring and representation theorists. We emphasize important roles of first extension groups of the preprojective algebra associated with a quiver.
